q-53580.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14238466/assets/7f5f82876a00c72d7ec829f320d021613d1932b85ef87c7981f9f92669792cb9.png)

Jessica's circular swimming pool has a radius of $10\,\text{ft}.$ What is the area of the pool?
q-53580.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of a circle is $A=\pi {r}^{2},$ so the area of Jessica's pool is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\pi \cdot {10}^{2} \\  & =100\pi \,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Jessica's circular swimming pool has a radius of 10ft. What is the area of the pool?

a
5ft2
b
25πft2
c
400ft2
d
10ft2
e
100πft2
Submit
Correct

q-79020.name: Question 2
q-79020.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14238466/assets/22f63e5e602b29317d7df70f7dae7387feccdd9ab5678592e6c1af35d3d45fd3.png)

What is the area of a circle that has a diameter of $8\,\text{m}?$
q-79020.worked_solution:
The radius of a circle is half the diameter. So, the radius of our circle is $r=4.$

Therefore, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\pi \cdot {4}^{2} \\  & =16\pi \,{\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

16πm2
c
64πm2
d
4πm2
e

q-79026.name: Question 3
q-79026.problem: What is the diameter of a circle if its area is $9\pi \,{\text{km}}^{2}?$
q-79026.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of a circle is $A=\pi {r}^{2}$, where $r$ is the radius. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\ 9\pi  & =\pi {r}^{2} \\ 9\cancel{\pi } & =\cancel{\pi }{r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =9 \\ r & =3\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the diameter is

$$
d=2\cdot r=2\cdot 3=6\,\text{km}.
$$

Question 3
?

What is the diameter of a circle if its area is 9πkm2?

a
4km
b
6πkm
c
6km
d
3km
e
9km
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the area of a circle is A=πr2, where r is the radius. Therefore,

A=πr29π=πr29π=πr2r2=9r=3km.

Therefore, the diameter is

d=2⋅r=2⋅3=6km.
